How AQMath Works — What the Calculations Mean and What You Decide

Published: 2026-08-07

Version: v3.0
Audience: every BLACK user, shown as a must-read before first use
Status: 📖 USER GUIDE — the single source of truth for the in-app explainer

1. What AQMath is (and is not)

AQMath is software for mathematical calculation. It computes figures from the assets, amounts and parameters you enter. It is not a trading bot, it never connects to any exchange, it holds no funds, and it never places an order. AQMath records, it does not decide: you make every decision and carry out any action yourself, on your own account, at your own discretion. Nothing happens without your manual action.

The figures are arithmetic results, not advice, not an instruction and not a recommendation. There is no guarantee of any outcome, and losses are possible in every market regime. The numbers AQMath shows come from mathematical risk models examined in backtests; backtests are simulated history, not a promise about the future.

2. The two loops

The MACRO loop — KKT risk parity (slow, frozen)

When you save your portfolio for the first time, the engine computes KKT risk-parity weights for your token set: each token receives a share of capital proportional to how much risk (not price movement) it contributes, subject to structural limits (per-token caps, at most 60% of capital in risky assets, the rest treated as stable reserve).

These weights are then frozen. They are not recomputed when you press a button and not recomputed when prices move. The only thing that changes them is the macro loop: every 180 days the engine re-optimises once and freezes the new weights. You are notified when this happens.

The daily loop — Proteus (v18) Deleverage Shield (fast, frozen configuration)

Once per day, after market close, the engine runs the Proteus (v18) Deleverage Shield over your frozen weights. The shield is a regime modulator: it reads the drawdown and downside volatility of your basket and continuously computes a target exposure between fully invested and defensive (more reserve, less risk). Its drawdown threshold is scaled by your basket's own trailing volatility, so one configuration adapts to calm and wild baskets alike. The configuration is frozen at Proteus (v18) — examined out-of-sample on the exact production path and no longer tuned. Portfolios with too little history to calibrate the adaptive threshold fall back to its fixed-threshold predecessor, Aegis (v14), until they have warmed up.

3. What a calculated difference means

After each daily run the engine compares the shield-adjusted theoretical weights with the holdings you declared. If the difference for a token is material, you receive a calculation notice that states it as a figure:

  • BTC: calculated difference −0.5 BTC ≈ −31,200 USD — your declared holding is above its theoretical weight by roughly this amount.
  • SOL: calculated difference +120 SOL ≈ +18,400 USD — your declared holding is below its theoretical weight by roughly this amount.

The amounts are computed from the prices and the portfolio value at run time. They describe the size and sign of a mathematical difference and nothing more: they contain no instruction and are not a recommendation. Whether you do anything about a figure, and how, is entirely your own decision; fees and slippage are yours to consider.

Notifications are deliberately rare. You only receive a message when:

1. the Deleverage Shield status turns ACTIVE (the computed target exposure is reduced), 2. the Deleverage Shield status turns back OFF, 3. a macro re-optimisation freezes new weights (every 180 days), 4. a material calculated difference is found, 5. the daily run fails — you are told the calculation did not run.

No message on ordinary days means the calculation found nothing material.

4. Your data

To personalise the calculation you declare which tokens you hold and in what amounts. These holdings are stored on our servers tied to the hash of your activation key, and are used only to compute your personal figures. You can update them any time, and deleting your key deletes your holdings, your consent records and your notification subscription. Full details are in the Privacy Policy.

5. Notifications

Notifications are delivered through our own first-party push server — no third-party provider sees your figures. You install the free ntfy app, add our server address and subscribe to your personal topic — no login or password is required, because the random 32-character topic name itself is your private address and is read-only. Turning notifications off closes the topic immediately; the calculations are still computed and logged in the app.

6. The honest summary

  • AQMath calculates the mathematical difference between your declared holdings and the theoretical model weights. Nothing more.
  • You decide what, if anything, to do with it — on your own account.
  • Weights are frozen at entry and re-optimised every 180 days; the shield recalculates the target exposure daily; both run without your intervention.
  • There is no guarantee. The shield reduces drawdowns in backtests; markets can still lose value, including rapidly.
